title: The Hot Classroom
activityInstruction: Drag each fan part into the build zone. It will snap into place with a fact.

storyQuestions.prompt: What happens when the child waves the book?
storyQuestions.success: The air moves when the child waves the book.

storyQuestions.prompt: Does the moving air feel good?
storyQuestions.success: Yes, the moving air feels good.
The child stops because their arm gets tired.

storyQuestions.prompt: What do the children want to do?
storyQuestions.success: The children want to make the air move.

storyQuestions.prompt: Do they want to keep using their hands?
storyQuestions.success: No, they do not want to keep using their hands.

quiz.prompt: Which part spins around to move the air?
quiz.success: The blade spins around to move the air.

quiz.prompt: Which part keeps your fingers away from the blade?
quiz.success: The guard keeps your fingers away from the blade.

quiz.prompt: Which part holds the fan steady so it does not tip over?
quiz.success: The base holds the fan steady.

quiz.prompt: Where is the motor on this fan?
answers: In the middle, behind the blade.
quiz.success: The motor sits in the middle, behind the blade.
The spinning blade makes the air move.

parts.label: Blade
parts.fact: The blades spin around to push the air and make a breeze.
parts.help: The orange shapes behind the fan guard.

parts.label: Motor
parts.fact: The motor turns the blades when the fan is switched on.
parts.help: The round hub in the middle of the fan.

parts.label: Stand
parts.fact: The stand holds the motor and blades above the base.
parts.help: The upright part between the base and motor.

parts.label: Base
parts.fact: The base holds the fan steady so it does not tip over.
parts.help: The stand at the bottom of the fan.
